title: Read an analog clock to the nearest 5 minutes; know 60 minutes make an hour

lesson.title: Reading a Clock to the Nearest Five Minutes

steps.say: You already know how to skip count, and that is the secret to reading a clock. Today we will use skip counting by fives to read the exact time on any round clock on the wall, like the one in your classroom.

A clock has two hands. The short, fat hand is the hour hand, and it tells us the hour. The long, skinny hand is the minute hand. Here is the neat part. Every time the minute hand moves from one number to the next number, five minutes go by. So we skip count by fives: five, ten, fifteen, twenty, and so on. There are twelve numbers, and twelve times five is sixty. That is why sixty minutes make one whole hour, one full trip around the clock.

visual.caption: One full trip around equals 60 minutes

steps.say: Let's read a real clock. It is almost time for the school bus. First look at the short hand. It is sitting between the two and the three, so the hour is two. We always use the smaller number it has already passed. Now look at the long hand. It points at the ten. Skip count by fives to get there: five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty-five, thirty, thirty-five, forty, forty-five, fifty. Or just think ten times five equals fifty. So the time is two fifty.

visual.caption: Hour hand past 2, minute hand on 10, so 2:50

steps.say: Here is the trap that catches lots of kids. That short hand was snuggled up really close to the three, so it is tempting to say three fifty. But that is not right. The hour hand only counts an hour once it has gone all the way past that number. It has not reached the three yet, so we are still inside the two o'clock hour. Think of it like your birthday. The day before you turn nine, you are still eight, even though you are so close. So the answer is two fifty, not three fifty.

visual.caption: Still 2 o'clock hour, because the hour hand has not passed 3

steps.say: So remember the two steps. Step one, read the short hand and take the smaller number it has already passed. Step two, skip count by fives around to the long hand. That gives you the time, every single time.

visual.caption: Hour hand past 7, minute hand on 5, so 7:25

lesson.answer: Short hand gives the hour it has already passed; long hand you skip count by fives, and twelve fives make sixty minutes, which is one hour.

practice.question: Ms. Yuanyuan checks the clock in the gym before hockey practice starts. The short hour hand is sitting between the four and the five, and the long minute hand is pointing right at the eight. Draw this clock if it helps you. What time is it? And careful, it is not five o'clock something!
practice.answer: It is 4:40. The hour hand has passed the 4 but not the 5, so the hour is 4. The minute hand is on the 8, and 8 times 5 equals 40 minutes.
